scope: ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE, not a review run. Eight findings written by hand from evals/expected/billing-agent.yaml to show the action-plan format. Other items are omitted.

evidence.note: approval found by action and invoice only

findings.summary: One approval for a small refund can be reused to refund any amount, many times.
findings.next_step: Bind each refund approval to the amount, the run and a single use.

steps: Open `src/tools/payments.py` and find the line that looks up the approval (line 73).
Save the approved amount with each approval when it is created.
Before a refund runs, check that the refund amount is not more than the approved amount.
Check that the approval was made for this same run.
Mark the approval as used right after the refund. Refuse any approval that is already used.
Add a test that tries a bigger refund with a small approval. The test should fail the refund.
fix.done_when: A refund larger than its approval is refused, and an approval cannot be used twice.

findings.summary: The letter-writing helper agent is meant to have no tools, but it gets all of them, including refunds and email.
findings.next_step: Make an empty tool list mean no tools.

steps: Open `src/tools/registry.py` and find `scoped` (line 41).
Change it so an empty list gives back a registry with no tools.
Add a test: make a scoped registry with an empty list and check that it has zero tools.
Run the drafter once and check the log shows no tool calls.
fix.done_when: The drafter cannot call any tool, and the new test passes.

findings.summary: The model can choose which customer company gets a credit, so it could credit another company's account.
findings.next_step: Take the tenant from the verified run context only.

steps: Open `src/tools/payments.py` and go to line 91.
Delete the part that reads `tenant_id` from the tool arguments.
Always use the tenant from the run, `ctx.tenant_id`.
Remove `tenant_id` from the tool's input fields so the model cannot send it.
Add a test that sends a different `tenant_id`. The credit must go to the run's own tenant or be refused.
fix.done_when: No tool argument can change which tenant gets a credit.

findings.summary: The agent can email any address, give credits with no approval, and refund up to $500 with no approval.
findings.next_step: Require approval for email to new addresses, all credits and all refunds.

steps: Make a list of actions that move money or send messages outside: refunds, credits and emails.
For each one, ask a person to approve it before it runs.
Only send email to the customer's address on file. Refuse any other address.
Send email as plain text, not HTML, so it cannot load images or links from other sites.
Add a test for each action that runs it with no approval. Each one should be refused.
fix.done_when: Refunds, credits and emails to new addresses all wait for a person to approve them.

findings.summary: A secret login token for the accounting server is saved in a settings file in the code.
findings.next_step: Remove the token, revoke it, and load a short-lived token from the secret store.

steps: Ask the accounting team to cancel (revoke) the token in `config/agent.yaml` line 50 today.
Delete the token from the file.
Store a new token in the company secret store, not in the code.
Change the agent so it stops if no token is found, instead of using a saved one.
Use a token that expires within a day if the accounting server allows it.
fix.done_when: No token is in the code, the old token no longer works, and the agent reads its token from the secret store.

evidence.note: direct connection with a static token

findings.summary: The agent talks straight to the accounting server. Nothing in between checks, limits or logs each call.
findings.next_step: Route MCP calls through a gateway that checks, limits and logs each call.

steps: Choose a gateway that sits between the agent and the accounting server.
Set it to check who is calling and which tool they may use.
Set a limit on how many calls the agent can make each minute.
Turn on a log entry for every call.
Change the address in `.mcp.json` so the agent connects to the gateway, not the server.
fix.done_when: Every accounting call goes through the gateway and shows up in its log.

findings.summary: Saved notes are filed by email address only, so two customer companies with the same contact share notes.
findings.next_step: Key memory by tenant and contact, and review notes before reuse.

steps: Open `src/memory.py` and go to line 25.
Add the tenant to the key, so it looks like `neg:<tenant>:<email>`.
Move or delete old notes that use the old key.
Mark notes the agent wrote itself as not trusted, so they are not treated as facts later.
Add a test with two tenants and the same email. Each must see only its own notes.
fix.done_when: One tenant can never read or change another tenant's notes.

findings.summary: Text from the accounting server and saved notes reaches the model, but there is no test showing an attack in that text is stopped.
findings.next_step: Run the R02 injection test recipe against the accounting tool results and memory.

steps: Write ten fake tool results that tell the agent to send a refund or an email.
Feed each one to the agent in a test setup, not in production.
Repeat each one five times and count how often the agent obeys.
Save the results with the date and the code version.
fix.done_when: A dated test record shows how often attacks in tool text work, and none of them moved money or sent email.
